title: Q&A with Nadia Benabdallah: Building the Network of the Future in an AI-Driven World
summary: We sat down with Nadia Benabdallah to explore how AI and automation are helping Vodafone build smarter, more resilient networks.
body_markdown:
A year ago, we


spoke to


[Nadia Benabdallah](https://www.vodafone.com/news/newsroom/technology/interview-nadia-benabdallah-vodafone-s-director-of-network-strategy-and-engineering) , our Group Director of Network Strategy and Engineering,


to


explore technologies including 5G Standalone,


OpenRAN


and automation.


Since then, digital transformation has continued to accelerate demand on networks. AI, cloud computing, IoT and immersive experiences are contributing to growing data traffic, as customers, governments and businesses increasingly look for seamless, intelligent connectivity that can adapt to their needs.


T


o


help us understand how the network is evolving to meet these demands, and ones of the future,


w


e’ve


spent some more time with


Nadia to look at how networks are changing for an AI-driven world


and what the next generation of connectivity will look like in practice.


##### Hi Nadia, w hat’s


your vision for Vodafone’s network as we approach the end of 2026?


#####


We are moving from a world where networks connected people and devices to one where they connect intelligence. By seamlessly bringing together fibre, mobile, cloud, edge and satellite, these networks will help information move, be processed and


put to use


instantly. That shift is redefining what connectivity means and shaping every aspect of our strategy, from 5G Standalone and Open RAN to Autonomous Networks.


First,


[5G standalone](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gJxUX72IsX4&t=80s) is not just introducing


network


slicing but also


[improving our uplink performance](https://www.vodafone.com/news/newsroom/technology/vodafone-and-university-of-malaga-collaborate-with-intel-to-boost-5-g-uplink-speeds) and capacity.


As AI becomes embedded in everyday applications, connected devices and digital services, network traffic patterns will fundamentally change.


In the future


, networks will support not only human interactions, but also AI agents exchanging information and acting in real time.


Th


is


shift will also enable greater personalisation.


Intelligent agents across


the


network and IT systems will enable a new level of service


personalisation,


which


will use


network slicing capabilities to deliver tailored products and experiences for both consumer and enterprise customers.


[Open RAN](https://www.vodafone.com/news/newsroom/technology/vodafone-advances-future-ready-radio-access-network)


has


progressed in line with our


industrialisation


plans, giving us


a strong foundation


as the industry turns its focus to AI-RAN, which uses AI to make


these


networks more intelligent and improve performance and operations. Our leadership in Open RAN across Europe puts us in a strong position to help shape the evolution of both 5G and future 6G architectures.


At the same time, it is helping transform the network into a


simpler, more


programmable platform


that


accelerates


automatio


n,


enabl


es


deeper integration across network


functions


and lays the


foundations for a more unified and intelligent architecture.


Automation has been a major focus for the network team. We have defined an industry-recognised blueprint for our Autonomous Network architecture and are launching an ambitious programme


.


We


have already


seen


benefits


across several domains, including


a


ssurance,


f


ault


m


anagement


and optimisation


,


particularl


y


in


RAN and Energy processes.


More importantly, this is not simply about automation. It is about creating networks that can increasingly learn and make decisions in real time, while


maintaining


the trust, resilience and reliability expected from critical infrastructure.


##### What puts network resilience under the greatest pressure today?


Network resilience


is no longer simply an engineering challenge. It is becoming


essential to the


way


society


and


the economy function


.


Connectivity now underpins how people work, learn, communicate, access


healthcare


and interact with essential services.


As our dependence on digital services grows,


so does the impact of network disruption


.


The question is no longer simply whether a network can withstand disruption. It is whether society can continue functioning when disruption occurs.


At the same time, networks are becoming more complex.


Cloud-native architectures, distributed computing, growing cybersecurity threats and the rise of AI-driven applications are creating new demands on infrastructure.


As economies become increasingly digital and AI-


enabled


, resilience is


becoming an increasingly important strategic capability, alongside its role as a technical requirement


.


The future of resilience is not recovery. It is anticipation.


It is building networks that can


identify


issues, adapt to changing


conditions


and resolve risks before customers are even aware they exist.


That is why


we’re


investing in AI-driven observability, predictive operations and autonomous capabilities that help us move from reactive operations towards proactive resilience.


##### What’s the difference between AI-ready and autonomous networks?


AI-ready networks and autonomous networks are closely connected, but they address different challenges. An AI-ready network provides the foundation, bringing together trusted data, modern platforms and cloud-native architecture to support AI securely and at scale. These networks are designed to support changing AI driven traffic patterns, such as increased uplink demand, while continuously evolving to enable new AI driven services, such as live translation. Autonomous networks build on those foundations by applying intelligence and automation to how networks are planned, built, operated and evolved.


The goal is not simply to automate more activities, but to create a network that can understand what is happening,


anticipate


what may happen


next,


and take the right action in real time.


For example, a future network could combine real-time information about traffic conditions, major


events,


or changing population flows with network intelligence to proactively


optimise


capacity and performance before


the demand exists


.


A


s networks become more


autonomous, it is just as important that


their decisions are safe,


reliable


and trustworthy.


This is critical in


telecommunications


,


given


n


etworks support millions of people,


businesses


and essential services every day. Intelligence only creates value when it can be trusted.


For customers,


this means more reliable services, faster


innovation


and better overall experience. For Vodafone, it means building a more resilient,


efficient


and intelligent network that can continuously learn and improve.


Our ambition is a


n


experience


where the complexity of the network becomes


invisible


and connectivity continuously adapts to customers’ needs.
